evidence.exact_quote: First-party bundled specialty Personas may be modified, disabled, and restored to default; user-created and imported specialty Personas may be edited or deleted; provider-native files are seed/import material only, and provider-native tools lists, WebFetch, WebSearch, protocol JSON examples, context-manager steps, KPI/SLA guarantees, polished completion claims, and benchmark model recommendations are migration inputs rather than literal PM built-in guarantees.

items.statement: The allowed mutations and the seed-only provider boundary are explicit, but the unit supplies no authorization matrix, persistence/version contract, import rejection behavior, deletion lifecycle, rollback rule, or executable oracle for these destructive and untrusted-input paths; those choices are not safe builder discretion.

evidence.exact_quote: PM-native bundled specialty prompts should be small and sharp, with most specialties around 250-500 words, complex cross-stack or strategy specialties around 450-700 words, internal/helper or narrow stack specialties around 180-350 words, and bodies focused on mission, when to use, when not to use, operating posture, response approach, useful heuristics, boundaries, and handoff expectations.

items.impact: Two bundles can materially violate the intended sharpness or exception policy while both claim conformance because category assignment, word-count tolerance, and the necessity exception have no test rule.
items.statement: The prompt bands and required content topics are stated as guidance, but no classifier determines which band applies, no tolerance defines 'around,' and no authority or evidence standard decides when excluded material is truly required.
items.title: Prompt normalization lacks a falsifiable conformance oracle

evidence.exact_quote: Specialty auto-resolution must be predictable: role/function axis outranks stack axis, operation type outranks repository language hints, review/audit roles outrank implementation roles for validation/governance/review tasks, implementation roles outrank review roles for build/change tasks, framework/tool specialists refine broader roles, fullstack-developer loses to narrower backend/frontend or stack-specific matches when justified, and governance/review/corroboration Personas do not collapse into implementation Personas because repository language hints are strong.

items.impact: The same inputs may resolve differently across builders, especially for mixed review/build requests, multiple narrow matches, concurrent override changes, or ambiguous strong matches, with no required reason trace for support.
items.statement: The precedence direction is useful but does not define normalized resolver inputs, tie-breaking among equal-axis candidates, thresholds for 'justified' or 'strongly matched,' snapshot behavior under changing overrides, fallback behavior, or an observable deterministic decision record.
items.title: Auto-resolution precedence is not fully deterministic

evidence.exact_quote: The specialty browser uses grouping and auto-resolution together: top-level group, specialty within group, optional stack/framework refinement, then project/global override.

items.impact: The browser can falsely imply an effective selection when data is stale, empty, loading, invalid, unavailable offline, or superseded by policy, and users may be unable to understand or operate the hierarchy accessibly.

segments.summary: Reviewed all P-044 through P-051 core lines and both structural and semantic refs. Exact strengths are the Collaborator confirmation gate, configurable-versus-protected catalog boundary, group hierarchy, exclusions, curated sets, prompt posture, and resolver precedence; adversarial gaps concentrate in mutation/import lifecycle, promotion propagation, prompt falsifiability, and deterministic resolver ties and provenance.

Reviewed all P-052 through P-054 core lines plus the intervening retired bridge and migration disposition. Exact strengths are browser ordering, registry ownership separation, protected and tweakable classes, workflow-profile reuse, specialist roles, and controller-only writes; gaps remain in truthful browser states, merge/reset concurrency, and enforceable specialist handoff contracts.
